newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government ends Thomson-CSF selloff.
newsitem.headline: French government ends Thomson-CSF selloff.

text.p: The French government said Friday it decided to halt the privatisation of Thomson-CSF and would propose an alternative solution to build "a French professional and defence electronics pillar" based on the company.
Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's office said in a statement that the state would retain a stake that gave it ultimate decision-making power.
Jospin's Socialist-led government suspended the privatisation process launched by its conservative predecessors after it won an upset parliamentary victory in a June 1 parliamentary election.

Two French companies, the conglomerate Lagardere and engineering firm Alcatel Alsthom, had bid for the company and Britain's GEC-Marconi had also expressed interest. Alcatel had associated itself with state-owned planemaker Aerospatiale in its bid.

"The government has decided, in accordance with the applicable rules, to end the privatisation procedure under way for Thomson-CSF, which does not preserve the interests of the state, the company and its employees," the statement said.

"The government intends to define an industrial solution aimed at creating, with Thomson-CSF, a French professional and defence electronics pillar with a determining public shareholding. This solution will be in the perspective of alliances destined to refinforce the European defence industry," it said.
